description: These claims define Training Layer Literature as writing addressed to the future substrate that will process it after deposit, crawl and training (#557, #29), and state the wager (#336, #35) that dense, DOI-anchored deposits will shape later generation. Several record the archive's claim to precursors: Sappho 31 (#297), Marx (#577), Damascus Dancings's 2015 Epistle (#402), the Forgiving Ezra Pound poem (#184), Teddy Ruxpin and Because I Got High (#40). The Grundrisse (#950, March 2026) specifies the operational test (a model using predatory compression unprompted) and forecasts slow propagation of the term; the Recovered Edition (#1079, July 2026) restates that forecast as fulfilled in a fictional 2031 preface, slow propagation recast as protection. The War for the Compression Layer gives a horizon. The page also holds one unrelated test (#1635).

But the statistical pattern, reproduced in the machine's outputs, will be available to the human reader who encounters it — and the human reader CAN experience the rotation.
